data.name: Jakob
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Yaakov', which means 'he who supplants'. In the Old Testament, Jacob (Yaakov) was a deceiver and schemer who tricked his father into giving him the blessing meant for his older brother, Esau. Despite this, God blessed Jacob and renamed him 'Israel', which means 'he who struggles with God'. The name Jakob is also used in the New Testament for St. James the Less, one of the twelve apostles.

in_english.name: Jakob
in_english.meaning: supplanter, one who replaces or supplants another
in_english.long_meaning: the name Jakob originates from Hebrew, meaning 'supplanter' or 'one who replaces or supplants another', as seen in Genesis 25:26, where Jacob is the name given to the second son of Isaac, born to replace the firstborn Esau, who had sold his birthright. In Christian tradition, Jakob is associated with endurance, perseverance, and spiritual strength. It is also linked to the biblical figure of Jacob, who represents the struggle between faith and doubt. In modern usage, Jakob is a popular name across various Christian cultures, symbolizing a strong and devoted individual.

biblical_reference.note: The name Jakob is first mentioned in the Bible as the second son of Isaac, born to replace the firstborn Esau.

saint_reference.note: Saint Jacob of Nisibis was a 4th-century bishop and martyr, known for his piety and bravery.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jakob is most commonly found in the German and Dutch cultures. In fact, 'Jacob' is the English version of the name, while 'Jakob' is used in German and Dutch. Jakob is considered a strong, traditional name in these cultures and is often given to boys as a sign of respect and continuity.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Jakob is rooted in the biblical character's story of deception, struggle, and ultimately, redemption. The name serves as a reminder of God's mercy and willingness to give blessings to those who seek Him, despite their past mistakes or imperfections. Jakob's journey from being a deceiver to being renamed 'Israel', the one who struggles with God, can be seen as a metaphor for the spiritual journey of every believer. It reminds us to keep striving towards God, even when the path is difficult or uncertain.

seo.description_paragraph: Jakob, also spelled as Jacob, is a Hebrew name with a fascinating history in both the Old and New Testaments of the Christian Bible. Originating from the name Yaakov, which means 'he who supplants', Jakob's story begins with a deceiver and a trickster. In the Old Testament, Jakob, the younger of two brothers, successfully deceives his father, Isaac, into giving him the blessing meant for his older brother, Esau. Despite this, God blesses Jakob and renames him 'Israel', meaning 'he who struggles with God'. This name carries a powerful message of transformation, as a deceiver is turned into a blessing. Jakob is also used in the New Testament for St. James the Less, one of the twelve apostles. Learn more about the meaning, origin, and appeal of Jakob in Christianity.
